grid.formula: Trust Score = sum over criteria of (sub-score / scale x weight): the five criteria scored out of 100 count sub-score x weight / 100; Roya's note, out of 25 with a weight of 25, counts point for point. Firms not traded with our own money are capped after the sum.
grid.subjectiveNote: Roya's note is the one subjective criterion in the grid: Roya's own rating after using the firm (interface, execution, support, feel), out of 25. The five others are documentary or measured. On firms we have not traded with our own money, it is an opinion formed without a paid account.

statusRecords.name: GT Funded
statusRecords.http: gtfunded.com: no DNS (10 Aug) · gtfunded.xyz: 307 → 200 (15 Sep)
statusRecords.note: The original domain has had no DNS record since June 2026 and never returned. A new site now runs on gtfunded.xyz under an 'AI-DeFi' positioning — but it is a waitlist landing page, not a working platform: the only call to action is 'Join Waitlist', there is no dashboard, and the page contradicts itself on maximum funding ($250K in the hero, $500K in the how-it-works section). It also advertises a '100% profit split' tier, which leaves no stated revenue model. Nothing on the site explains what happened to traders funded before the shutdown. Treat as unproven, not as a returning firm. Re-read 15 September 2026: still the same waitlist page ('Join 2,400+ traders on the waitlist'), counters rendered at 0. Re-read 26 September 2026: www.gtfunded.xyz answers 307 → 200 and the page's own metadata now advertises 'funded up to $500K', 'keep up to 90% of profits' and 'no KYC, no middlemen' — a larger promise than the $250K hero of eleven days earlier, on a page that still shows no platform. Its Open Graph URL and preview image still resolve to gtfunded.vercel.app. The body renders client-side and returned no content to our reader that day, so the call to action was NOT confirmed on 26 September; the last confirmed read of a waitlist-only page remains 15 September 2026.

statusRecords.name: FundedPoly
statusRecords.http: Vercel 'Deployment Paused' page (15 Sep) · 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED (25 Jul, 10 Aug)
statusRecords.note: The domain resolves but the site returns HTTP 402 'Payment Required' with Vercel's DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED error — the hosting is suspended, typically for non-payment. The firm was still advertising funded Polymarket accounts with an 80% split and up to 3x leverage. Status unclear: this may be a billing lapse or the first stage of a shutdown. The same 402 was returned on 25 July and again on 10 August — the longer it lasts, the less it looks like a billing accident. Do not buy an evaluation until it is back up. Re-read 15 September 2026: the domain now serves Vercel's 'This deployment is temporarily paused' page, title 'Deployment Paused' — no product visible, seven weeks after the first 402. Re-checked 26 September 2026: HTTP 402 again on the automated sweep, and a direct read of fundedpoly.com returned an empty body — sixty-three days after the first 402 of 25 July 2026. A two-month suspension is no longer readable as a billing accident, but we do not mark a firm dead on hosting alone: it stays at risk.

statusRecords.name: Hypernova
statusRecords.note: Operational and public since 14 August 2026 — checkout open on app.hypernova.xyz with published pricing ($120/$275/$365 on the 25K account; pricing unchanged across five checks through 31 August). Hyperliquid-native, with programmatic smart-contract payouts and an on-chain payout reserve. Its own documentation states up to an 80% split, not the 90% repeated on comparison sites — a split we have now reconciled first-hand: 11 payouts (3,660.86 USDC) taken on our own funded account 28 August – 1 September 2026, each reconciled on-chain, one checked at exactly 80% to the cent. Reserve reading of 31 August 2026, 03:18 UTC: $744,569.83 on Arbitrum (vault + reserve wallet), after a $861,517.34 top-up level on 25 August; the homepage displayed a rounded $765.5K the same day — it no longer matches the chain to the cent. Homepage re-read 15 September 2026: reserve shown $958.4K, lifetime payouts $852.8K, average payout 5.9 s. Homepage and /stats re-read 26 September 2026: payout reserve $600,015 (cold reserve + operational vault on Arbitrum), down $358,384 — 37.4% — from the $958,399.39 shown eleven days earlier, against $1,003,923 paid out over the trailing 30 days on the same page. Lifetime payouts $1,190,239 across 219 recipients, 94 funded traders, $4.43M funded-trader AuM, average payout $963, largest $8,000. The site now publishes its own pass rate — 22.6%, 718 of 3,180 resolved assessments, and by account size from 16.5% ($10K) to 27.6% ($100K) — plus a median account lifespan of 0.8 days. The homepage carries a 'closed beta · invite only' badge, a $200K funding ceiling and rulebook v1.1; pricing on the 25K account unchanged at $120/$275/$365. Its own FAQ states every trade runs in a simulated account. A reserve falls when traders get paid and also when a treasury moves money; we did not trace the outflows and read no cause into them. Status unchanged: active.

changelog.title: Hypernova reserve down $169,194.50 in four days: $958,399.39 (15 Sep) → $789,204.89 (19 Sep)
changelog.body: Daily 03:00 UTC on-chain readings of Hypernova's payout reserve on Arbitrum (vault + reserve wallet): $958,399.39 on 15 September, $925,592.74 on 16 September, $870,858.82 on 17 September, $849,504.79 on 18 September, $789,204.89 on 19 September 2026 — a fall of $169,194.50, or 17.7%, in four days. The reserve wallet moved from $931,255.04 to $758,255.04 in that window; the operational vault stayed between $14K and $31K. We did not trace the destinations of the outflows and we are not reading a cause into them: a reserve that pays traders goes down when traders get paid, and it also goes down when a treasury moves money. Status unchanged: active. Every reading, with its block number, is on the reserve tracker.

changelog.title: Correction: three days of false 'no DNS record' readings withdrawn — full hand re-check of all 10 firms, no status change
changelog.body: From 13 to 15 September 2026 our automated daily sweep recorded 'dns: no-record' for every tracked domain, live firms included, and that reading reached registry.json and the register table. It was false: the sites were up. The cause was our resolver call (Node's dns.resolve4, which talks to DNS servers directly) failing on the machine that runs the sweep while ordinary HTTPS requests succeeded — a tooling fault on our side, not a change at any firm. Fixed the same day: the sweep now falls back to the operating-system resolver, aborts when a known-good name fails to resolve, and refuses to write a run in which every domain came back dark. The false readings were discarded and all 10 pages were re-read by hand in a browser on 15 September 2026: no status changes. FundedPoly now serves Vercel's 'This deployment is temporarily paused' page (seven weeks after its first HTTP 402); gtfunded.xyz is still a waitlist landing page; the other eight are up. As always, no verdict moved on an automated reading.

changelog.title: Correction: Carrot Funding reclassified active — our 10 Aug 'dead' verdict checked the wrong domain
changelog.body: On 10 August we classified Carrot Funding dead because carrotfunding.com 302-redirects to a HugeDomains parking page. That was the wrong domain: the firm brands itself carrotfunding.io and is fully operational there — challenge checkout live ($5K to $100K), 80% split, USDC payouts on Arbitrum with published transaction hashes. Status corrected to active, checked 15 August 2026. Two lessons enter the methodology: a death verdict must name the exact domain checked, and we search a firm's socials and docs for alternative official domains before classifying. Separately noted: Carrot's advertised ceiling is now $100K, down from the $500K seen in July, with no announcement.

changelog.title: Registry opened: 10 crypto prop firms under dated DNS/HTTP monitoring
changelog.body: First dated checks recorded for the crypto prop firm status registry: every tracked firm — living ones included — gets DNS resolution, HTTP status and a manual read of the live page, each check dated.
